topic_brief.title: No-till vs conventional tillage effects on crop yield
topic_brief.research_question: Does no-till management affect crop yield compared to conventional tillage, and how does this vary by crop type and climate?
topic_brief.population_description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing tillage systems
topic_brief.intervention_description: No-till or zero-till management (seeds planted directly into undisturbed soil)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional tillage (moldboard plow, disk, chisel, or other inversion/intensive tillage)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is NO-TILL (less disturbance), Control is CONVENTIONAL TILLAGE (more disturbance)
Reduced tillage is NOT no-till - if both exist, compare no-till vs conventional
Some papers have 3+ tillage levels - extract the no-till vs most intensive tillage comparison
Strip-till is intermediate - do not include as no-till unless paper explicitly calls it no-till
Long-term trials may show different effects in early vs late years - extract each year separately
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall -5.7%; Wheat -2.6%; Maize -7.6%; Rice -7.5%; Soybean +0.3%; Oilseed rape -9.0%

rows.title: Study of fuel consumption in three tillage methods
rows.treatment_description: No-tillage using direct drill planter (Ozdoken Model 2007), working depth 20 cm, no soil disturbance
rows.control_description: Maximum (conventional) tillage: moldboard plow + tandem disk harrow (3 stages) + leveler + seed planter, working depth 30 cm
rows.notes: Yield significantly different between tillage systems (ANOVA F=9.60, p<0.05). Duncan's test groups max. tillage in class 1 and no-tillage in class 2, confirming significant difference. MSE=0.07125 computed from ANOVA error SS=0.285 with df=4 (pooled across all 3 tillage systems). Pooled SD=sqrt(MSE)=0.267 t/ha. Farm previously used for corn, causing soil compaction and hard pan which authors note negatively affected no-till planter performance. Paper primarily focused on fuel consumption, yield is secondary outcome.

rows.title: Cover crops and herbicide timing management on soybean yield under no-tillage system
rows.treatment_description: No-tillage, fallow (no cover crop), mean across 4 herbicide timings (0, 10, 20, 30 days before sowing)
rows.control_description: Conventional tillage, fallow (weeds incorporated 30 days before soybean sowing)
rows.notes: NTS fallow mean averaged across 4 herbicide timings (12 subplot observations from 3 blocks). CTS fallow had lowest yield of all treatments. Large positive effect likely reflects poor CTS fallow performance rather than pure tillage effect. CV for yield = 9.21%. Area under NTS for 6 years prior (2001-2007).

moderators.mod_region: Santo Antônio de Goiás, GO, Brazil
moderators.mod_residue_management: fallow - weeds left on surface (NTS) vs incorporated (CTS)
moderators.mod_crop_rotation: corn-soybean rotation with cover crops, fallow in winter
moderators.mod_n_fertilizer_rate: not reported for soybean; 80 kg/ha P2O5+K2O applied

rows.title: Cover crops and herbicide timing management on soybean yield under no-tillage system
rows.treatment_description: No-tillage, Urochloa brizantha cover crop, mean across 4 herbicide timings
rows.control_description: Conventional tillage, U. brizantha incorporated 30 days before soybean sowing
rows.notes: Matched cover crop comparison (U. brizantha under both tillage systems). NTS mean averaged across 4 herbicide timings. Both treatments produced yields above national average (2823 kg/ha). CV = 9.21%. This is the cleanest no-till vs conventional comparison in this paper.

moderators.mod_region: Santo Antônio de Goiás, GO, Brazil
moderators.mod_residue_management: U. brizantha retained on surface (NTS) vs incorporated (CTS)
moderators.mod_crop_rotation: corn-soybean rotation, U. brizantha intercropped with corn (Santa Fé system)
moderators.mod_n_fertilizer_rate: not reported for soybean; 80 kg/ha P2O5+K2O applied

rows.title: Effect of tillage and crop residue management practices on yield and economics of wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) under conservation agriculture
rows.treatment_description: T1 - Zero tillage (direct seeding without soil disturbance using zero-till-seed-drill)
rows.control_description: T3 - Conventional tillage (one deep ploughing + two passes of cultivator with planking + normal seed drill)
rows.notes: Split plot design with 3 reps x 5 residue subplot treatments = 15 plots per tillage level. SE± = 82 is the SE of the tillage main effect mean. CD at 5% = 248; T1 vs T3 difference (257 kg/ha) exceeds CD so is significant. Reduced tillage (T2 = 2207 kg/ha) was at par with T3 and significantly higher than T1. T×R interaction was NS so individual cell means not reported. Paper reports only main effect means averaged over subplot treatments.
